answer: Dielectric-droplet attestation curbs Sybil attacks by binding each AI agent to a micro-electrode grid on a silicon island. A capillary quill spots random polymer droplets on the pads before opaque raven epoxy seals the die. To sign a verifier nonce, the chip measures AC capacitance across the pad array to reconstruct its signing key. Attackers must fabricate and enroll a separate chip per identity instead of cloning VMs. However, a dishonest foundry could record raw responses before sealing.
